title: Composition of K-injective-normalized derived comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B_i$ for $i=0,1,2$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Assume every complex of each $\mathcal A_i$ admits a K-injective resolution, i.e. a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes. Let $F_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B_i$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with total right derived functors $(RF_i,\eta^i)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $Q_i:K(\mathcal A_i)\to D(\mathcal A_i)$ and $P_i:K(\mathcal B_i)\to D(\mathcal B_i)$ for localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$ put $c^i_a=(\eta^i_I)^{-1}\circ RF_i(Q_i a)$, the canonical resolution identification [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation].

For $0\leq i<j\leq2$ let $r_{ij}:\mathcal A_j\to\mathcal A_i$ and $s_{ij}:\mathcal B_j\to\mathcal B_i$ be exact additive functors, also denoting their termwise derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Suppose $r_{02}=r_{01}r_{12}$, $s_{02}=s_{01}s_{12}$ and $F_i r_{ij}=s_{ij}F_j$ on objects and morphisms. Use the induced canonical localization identifications throughout.

Suppose natural isomorphisms $\beta_{ij}:RF_i r_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{ij}RF_j$ are given and have the following normalization. For every K-injective $H$ in $\mathcal A_j$ and every K-injective resolution $a:r_{ij}H\to I$ in $\mathcal A_i$, the map $P_i(F_i a)$ is invertible and
$$(s_{ij}\eta^j_H)^{-1}\circ\beta_{ij,Q_jH}\circ(c^i_a)^{-1}=P_i(F_i a)^{-1}.$$
Then for every $L\in D(\mathcal A_2)$,
$$\beta_{02,L}=s_{01}(\beta_{12,L})\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}.$$
No $r_{ij}$ is assumed to preserve K-injective complexes.
